T5A02: Power is measured in watts. Watt-hours measure energy, not power.
T5A05: Voltage is the push: a difference in voltage makes electrons flow.
T5A06: Frequency is measured in hertz (cycles per second).
T5A07: Metals conduct well because they have many free electrons.
T5A08: Glass is an insulator. Sea water, steel, and graphite all conduct.
T5A09: AC alternates between positive and negative directions.
T5A10: Power = the rate at which energy is used.
T5A11: Resistance opposes all of them: DC, AC, and RF current.
T5B07: MHz to kHz: multiply by 1000. 3.525 MHz = 3525 kHz.
T5B08: 1,000,000 pF = 1 uF (pico to micro is a factor of a million).
T5B10: 12 W to 3 W is a quarter of the power: half (-3 dB) twice = -6 dB.
T5B12: kHz to MHz: divide by 1000. 28400 kHz = 28.400 MHz.
T5B13: MHz to GHz: divide by 1000. 2425 MHz = 2.425 GHz.
T5C01: Capacitance stores energy in an electric field.
T5C03: Inductance stores energy in a magnetic field.
T5C05: Impedance is measured in ohms, like resistance.
T5C06: Kilohertz is written kHz: lowercase k, capital H.
T5C07: Megahertz is written MHz: capital M (lowercase m means milli).
T5C08: Power: P = I x E (current x voltage). Memory hook: PIE.
T5C12: Impedance = opposition to AC current flow.
T5D01: Ohm's law: I = E / R. Cover the letter you want in the E-over-I-R triangle.
T5D02: Ohm's law: E = I x R.
T5D10: E = I x R = 0.5 x 2 = 1 V.
T5D13: In a series circuit there's one path, so the current is the same everywhere.
T5D14: In a parallel circuit every branch connects across the same two points, so the voltage is the same.
T6A02: A volume control is a potentiometer (a variable resistor).
T6A04: A capacitor stores energy in an electric field.
T6A05: Two conductive plates separated by an insulator = a capacitor.
T6A06: An inductor stores energy in a magnetic field.
T6A07: A coil of wire = an inductor.
T6A08: SPDT (single pole, double throw): one circuit switched between two others.
T6A09: Component 3 in T-2 is a simple on/off switch: single-pole single-throw.
T6A10: All three are rechargeable: NiMH, lithium-ion, and lead-acid.
T6A11: Carbon-zinc (cheap dry cells) is not rechargeable.
T6B01: Forward voltage drop varies by diode type (about 0.3 V Schottky, 0.7 V silicon).
T6B02: A diode lets current flow in only one direction.
T6B03: A transistor can act as an electronic switch.
T6B04: A transistor has three regions of semiconductor (NPN or PNP).
T6B05: Gate, drain, and source = a field-effect transistor (FET). Bipolar is base, collector, emitter.
T6B06: A diode's cathode end is marked with a stripe.
T6B07: Forward current makes an LED light up.
T6B09: A diode's electrodes are the anode and cathode.
T6B10: A transistor can give power gain. Transformers and resistors can't.
T6B11: Gain can mean all of these: output vs. input voltage, current, or power.
T6B12: A bipolar transistor has an emitter, base, and collector.
T6C01: A diagram drawn with standard component symbols is a schematic.
T6C02: T-1 component 1, the zigzag, is a resistor.
T6C03: T-1 component 2, the circle with the bar and arrow, is a transistor.
T6C04: T-1 component 3, the dome-shaped symbol, is a lamp.
T6C05: T-1 component 4, long and short parallel lines, is a battery.
T6C06: T-2 component 6, one straight plate and one curved plate, is a capacitor.
T6C07: T-2 component 8, a diode with arrows pointing out (light), is an LED.
T6C08: T-2 component 9, a zigzag with an arrow, is a variable resistor.
T6C09: T-2 component 4, two coils with a core between them, is a transformer.
T6C10: T-3 component 3, a coil with an arrow tap, is a variable inductor.
T6C11: T-3 component 4, the triangle on a stick, is an antenna.
T6C12: Schematics show how components are connected. Not wire lengths or what parts look like.
T6D01: A rectifier turns AC into a varying DC.
T6D02: A relay is an electrically controlled switch.
T6D03: Shielded wire keeps unwanted signals from coupling into or out of the wire.
T6D04: A meter displays an electrical quantity as a number.
T6D05: A regulator controls a power supply's output voltage.
T6D06: A transformer steps 120 V AC down to a lower AC voltage.
T6D07: An LED is the common visual indicator.
T6D08: An inductor plus a capacitor = a resonant circuit.
T6D09: Many components in one package = an integrated circuit.
T6D10: T-1 component 2 is the transistor. It controls the flow of current (switching the lamp).
T6D11: A resonant (tuned) circuit = an inductor and a capacitor, in series or in parallel.
